newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks bolstered by industrials demand.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks bolstered by industrials demand.

text.p: Jordanian shares rose slightly on Monday in mainly locally driven demand on blue-chip industrials expected to post healthy half-year earnings, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose a slight 0.04 percent to 166.66 points in 1.2 million dinar turnover ($1.7 million), dominated by a few large deals.
The busiest traded stock, Jordan Cement Factories rose 0.05 dinars to 3.99 dinars in 352,980 dinars worth of trade rumoured to have been mainly foreign-inspired.
A large bloc deal in Bank of Jordan worth 254,980 dinars helped bolster volume in an otherwise steady market bolstered by interest in leading blue-chips.
Heavyweight Arab Bank, which drove the official index up to a three-year high earlier in July, shed 1 dinar to 293 dinars in only 20 share trade.
Local investors piled into the shares in recent weeks, anticipating strong 1997 profits, announcements of a bonus share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
Other stocks which saw some demand were Shipping Lines and El Zay garments manufacturer, rising 0.09 dinars to 3.05 dinars and 0.07 dinars to 1.44 dinars respectively.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, rose 0.20 percent to 81.07 points, 2.79 percent down since the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
